boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Trinity spaces for focused work, collaboration, and low-key campus time, grounded in Trinity’s library and campus sources.

cards.title: Settle into the library’s coffee-shop-style corner
cards.subtitle: Coates Library, Trinity University
cards.notes: Use the Starbucks seating when you want a relaxed setting to read or catch up on coursework; the library identifies it as a place to study and unwind.
cards.short_summary: A casual study setting inside Coates Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library describes its Starbucks area as a place to relax, unwind, and study.
cards.access_notes: Located within Coates Library; consult library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Take a living-room-style study break
cards.subtitle: Coates Library, third floor
cards.notes: Bring a book or laptop to the third-floor couches and chairs for an individual work session or a conversation with classmates.
cards.short_summary: Soft seating for solo work or studying with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library says its third-floor couches and chairs support hanging out with friends or studying alone.
cards.access_notes: Located within Coates Library; consult library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Choose the quiet-zone tables for deep work
cards.subtitle: Coates Library, second floor
cards.notes: Head to the designated quiet area when you need room to spread out and concentrate; keep conversations elsewhere to respect the zone.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet study area with roomy tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library identifies the second-floor quiet area as a quiet zone with roomy tables for studying.
cards.access_notes: Located within Coates Library; consult library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Work alongside Trinity’s rare books and archives
cards.subtitle: Coates Library, Room 208
cards.notes: Visit Room 208 for class research using manuscripts, rare books, or University Archives materials; check the unit’s separate hours before planning.
cards.short_summary: An archival research space in Coates Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library says Special Collections in Room 208 includes manuscripts, rare books, and Trinity University Archives.
cards.access_notes: Special Collections has separate hours; confirm access before visiting.

cards.title: Configure a study setup that fits the task
cards.subtitle: Coates Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the Zen Den’s movable furniture to build a solo or small-group setup with booths, stools, tables, chairs, and partitions.
cards.short_summary: Flexible first-floor study furniture for different work styles.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library describes the first-floor Zen Den as a modular-furniture study area with booths, stools, tables, chairs, and partitions.
cards.access_notes: Located within Coates Library; consult library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Claim a window-side corner table
cards.subtitle: Coates Library
cards.notes: Look for the corner study spots when daylight helps you focus; they offer floor-to-ceiling natural light while you work through an assignment.
cards.short_summary: Window-side study tables with natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library describes its corner study spots as tucked-away areas with floor-to-ceiling natural light.
cards.access_notes: Located within Coates Library; consult library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Reserve a room for focused group work
cards.subtitle: Coates Library
cards.notes: Reserve a private study room for individual or group work, especially early during midterms and finals when the library notes demand increases.
cards.short_summary: Reservable private rooms for individual or group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library offers private study rooms for individuals and groups through an online reservation system.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; availability varies, particularly around midterms and finals.

cards.title: Browse for a study carrel or tucked-away seat
cards.subtitle: Coates Library
cards.notes: Walk the building and try a study carrel or another tucked-away seat when you want a change from open tables and shared lounges.
cards.short_summary: Scattered study carrels and smaller library work areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library says study carrels and other tucked-away study spots are available throughout the building.
cards.access_notes: Located within Coates Library; consult library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Use Trinity’s central pedestrian route
cards.subtitle: Between Coates Student Center and Murchison Hall
cards.notes: Take the Esplanade between lower-division residence halls and upper campus, pausing at its seating areas or using the improved Wi-Fi for a quick reset.
cards.short_summary: An accessible central route with seating and event lighting.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the Coates Esplanade connects lower-division residence halls and upper campus and includes seating, Wi-Fi, and pedestrian lighting.
cards.access_notes: Trinity reported the Esplanade fully open and accessible on February 14, 2025.

cards.title: Meet up in the renovated co-working area
cards.subtitle: Trinity University campus
cards.notes: Use the Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship’s student co-working area for project conversation, then shift to its informal meeting area when a smaller discussion helps.
cards.short_summary: A renovated co-working and informal meeting space.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity reports that its Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship reopened with a student co-working area and informal meeting area.
cards.source_title: Building the Engine that Runs the Center
cards.access_notes: The space supports Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship activities; verify current visitor access with the center.
